item.description: The base NotifyBase class has inconsistent handling of plugin instantiation and URL parsing that leads to failures in URL-based plugin loading.
item.contract: Ensure that all plugin classes properly implement the `parse_url` method and handle URL parsing consistently with the base class. The `instantiate` method in Apprise class should properly handle all plugin instantiation scenarios including missing parameters and invalid configurations.
item.acceptance: tests/test_plugin_dapnet.py::test_plugin_dapnet_urls, tests/test_plugin_telegram.py::test_plugin_telegram_urls, and similar URL parsing test cases should pass.

item.description: Missing or incomplete template definitions in plugin classes cause test failures related to URL building and validation.
item.contract: All plugin classes must properly define `templates` and `template_tokens` attributes that are used for URL parsing and building. The `templates` attribute should be a tuple of URL format strings and `template_tokens` should define all required parameters.
item.acceptance: Tests that check template parsing and URL building should pass for multiple plugins like tests/test_plugin_dapnet.py, tests/test_plugin_telegram.py, etc.

item.description: The `instantiate` method in Apprise class has inadequate error handling for plugin initialization failures.
item.contract: The `instantiate` method should properly handle instantiation failures by catching exceptions and returning None instead of crashing. It should also ensure that plugins with missing or invalid dependencies are properly handled.
item.acceptance: tests/test_api.py::test_apprise_disabled_plugins and similar tests should pass when plugins are disabled or have missing dependencies.

item.description: Missing or improperly defined `enabled` property in plugin classes causes issues with plugin activation and test failures.
item.contract: Plugins must properly implement the `enabled` class property to control whether they are active. The default should be True, and it should be set appropriately based on environment conditions.
item.acceptance: Tests checking for disabled plugins should pass, and the plugin manager should properly recognize enabled/disabled states.

item.description: Inconsistent handling of the `requirements` class variable across plugin implementations.
item.contract: Plugins should properly define the `requirements` class variable with correct structure. Missing or incorrectly formatted requirements should not cause instantiation failures.
item.acceptance: Tests checking for plugin requirements and dependency validation should pass for all plugins.
